title: Ribbon runs: Threshold file
summary: A run is a maximal consecutive group of identical characters. Produce its length for each run, from left to right. Spaces are characters too. Return how many values in the derived sequence are at least k.
descriptionMd:
A sticking key leaves repeated marks across a typewriter ribbon's inspection strip. Neri marks a threshold on the filing cabinet's inspection card. Only qualifying readings count toward today's clearance stamp.

A run is a maximal consecutive group of identical characters. Produce its length for each run, from left to right. Spaces are characters too.

Return how many values in the derived sequence are at least k.

Implement ribbonRunsThresholdFile(line, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: String runs. A run is a maximal consecutive group of identical characters. Produce its length for each run, from left to right. Spaces are characters too. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys (earlier units are used while the first two levels establish the foundations).
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
The line contains ASCII characters; the only word separator is a space.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with string runs. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

A run is a maximal consecutive group of identical characters. Produce its length for each run, from left to right. Spaces are characters too. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return how many values in the derived sequence are at least k. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [1,1,2,1,1,3,1,1,1]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are at least k. This gives 1.
The derived sequence is [2,1,1,2]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are at least k. This gives 2.
The derived sequence is []. Return how many values in the derived sequence are at least k. This gives 0.

overview: Edge-case trap: String runs. Build the sequence once, then report exactly what the inspection card requests.
